concept_name: The Rotational Second Law — τ = Iα
source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.7 System of Particles and Rotational Motion — table-of-contents scope only (tau = I alpha is a named NCERT-section topic); teaching authored from first principles. The atomic concept: a net external torque produces angular acceleration in proportion, tau_net = I alpha — torque sets how quickly the spin rate CHANGES, never the spin rate itself, and the same torque produces less alpha when I is larger. Does NOT cover what torque is or the moment arm (torque, not yet shipped), how I is computed or its axis-dependence (moment_of_inertia, not yet shipped), the kinematics omega = omega0 + alpha t as its own subject (rotational_kinematics), rotational work/energy (rotational_work_energy), or angular momentum L and its conservation (angular_momentum / conservation_of_angular_momentum — L, KE, dL/dt and F_pull readouts are never shown in this concept). Built on the rigid_body_rotation field_3d engine (build 0c-3, docs/loop_runs/rotmech/_engine/findings_d.md), pure configuration, zero renderer edits.

real_world_anchor.primary: Pushing a playground merry-go-round: hold a steady push on the rail and it does not turn at one speed — it keeps speeding up for as long as you keep pushing.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The same merry-go-round with riders sitting near the edge: the same steady push speeds it up more slowly, because the riders sitting farther out add more inertia.

r.name: Radius of each sliding mass from the axle — a restart-seed-only pose in every guided state (never ramps concurrently with an engaged torque in S1-S7); live-drivable only in S8

m.name: Mass of each sliding mass (two, symmetric about the axle) — fixed at 2.0 kg in every guided state; live-drivable only in S8

omega0.name: Seed angular speed magnitude at state entry / restart — sets omega at t=0 for a state or an S5 run-cut / S8 restart; never applied as a continuous drive (that is tau_app's job)

omega.name: Live angular speed — the derived quantity omega = L/I, recomputed every step; never itself an independent variable or slider

tau_app.name: Applied drive torque magnitude via the motor drive wheel at the rim — the TAUGHT variable; the wheel translates in and its rim arrow tracks this value; contact = the engage instant. Core-ring control at S8 (engine token tau_applied)

tau_brake.name: Brake torque MAGNITUDE while the pad is engaged against the drum rim — frictional: opposes the EXISTING sign of omega, decelerates only, never reverses at any reachable value

I_frame.name: Fixed inertia of the turntable + rod, excluding the two sliding masses

R_drum.name: Braked / driven radius — where the pad and the motor drive wheel both contact the turntable's rim

rod_half_length.name: Rod half-length — apparatus geometry only, not a formula input

rod_height_above_pad.name: Vertical clearance of the rod plane above the drum's pad plane — apparatus geometry only

alpha.name: Angular acceleration — the per-step finite difference (omega_k - omega_k_minus_1)/h on the fixed 16 ms grid, published from the SAME post-step snapshot as I/omega/tau, blanked across every re-pin/restart window. The shared chapter definition (findings_d.md section 1); equal to tau_net/I exactly whenever I is constant (every guided beat here)

tau.name: Net torque displayed on the HUD — the NET RESOLVED torque the integrator actually used at t, never the authored schedule value (P1-A). Satisfies tau = I*alpha identically at every instant, including S6's rest clamp (tau -> 0.00 with alpha -> 0.00 while the pad stays engaged) and S8's static hold
tau.derived: tau = I * alpha (identically, at every instant, by construction of the P1-A remedy)

I.formula: I(t) = I_frame + 2*m*r(t)^2 — recomputed live; held fixed for the duration of any engaged torque

F_drive.formula: F_drive = tau_app / R_drum — the rim tangential force arrow's printed label

formulas.newtons_second_law_rotational: tau_net = I*alpha — the ONE law this concept teaches. Closed form: L(t+h) = L(t) + tau_net_resolved(t)*h; omega(t) = L(t)/I(t) recomputed every step; alpha(t) = (omega_k - omega_k_minus_1)/h on the fixed 16 ms grid
formulas.drive_torque_source: tau_drive_term = +tau_app while the motor drive wheel is in contact (engage = contact); 0 otherwise. Never authored against the existing spin direction in this concept — the sign law is taught by the BRAKE (S6), not by a reversed drive
formulas.brake_torque_source: tau_brake_term = -sign(omega)*tau_brake while the pad is engaged (frictional, opposes the EXISTING spin only); 0 otherwise. Decelerates toward rest; never reverses spin at any reachable tau_brake value
formulas.net_torque_resolved: tau_net_resolved(t) = sum of every currently-engaged source's signed contribution, including the S8 static-hold case: while the brake is engaged and the drive magnitude is at most tau_brake, tau_net_resolved = 0 exactly
formulas.drive_force_at_rim: F_drive = tau_app / R_drum. S2: 2.78 N at R_drum = 0.55 m gives 2.78*0.55 = 1.53 N*m. S4: 1.09 N gives 1.09*0.55 = 0.60 N*m
formulas.predicted_speed_kinematics_patch: omega = omega0 + alpha*t — the one-breath S4 kinematics patch, spoken only, never a second formula surface
formulas.per_particle_derivation: S7 only: F_t = m*r*alpha = 2.0*0.80*0.50 = 0.80 N per mass, equal by symmetry; tau_per_mass = m*r^2*alpha = 2.0*0.64*0.50 = 0.64 N*m; tau_frame_term = I_frame*alpha = 0.50*0.50 = 0.25 N*m; tau = (Sigma m*r^2 + I_frame)*alpha = 0.64+0.64+0.25 = 1.53 = I*alpha exactly

constraints: tau_net = I times alpha identically, at every instant — including the rest clamp and the S8 static hold. The tau readout displays the RESOLVED value the integrator used, never the authored schedule value (P1-A, binding)
alpha is the per-step finite difference of omega on the fixed 16 ms grid, blanked across every re-pin/restart window — never an independently integrated quantity

The brake is frictional: opposes the existing sign of omega, decelerates only, never reverses spin at any reachable tau_brake value. A sustained DRIVEN opposing torque genuinely CAN reverse a spin (real physics, out of this concept's scope, owned by the sibling sandbox) — never plant the belief that an opposing torque can never reverse a spin
I(t) = I_frame + 2*m*r(t)^2 is held fixed for the duration of any engaged torque in every guided state — r changes only between drives, never concurrently with an engaged torque

omega = 0 with both drive and brake engaged (S8) is a static hold with breakaway, not a limit case: while the brake magnitude is at least the drive, L is held at exactly 0 and sign(L) is never consulted
r is in the range 0.15 to 0.90 m; every authored pose (0.20, 0.50, 0.80) sits strictly inside it

The taught law is a proportion, never an equality of magnitude across states — the SAME tau (1.53 N.m) produces different alpha depending on I; no narration states or implies same torque, same acceleration
KE, L, dL/dt and F_pull readouts are NEVER shown in this concept — showing L would pre-spoil angular_momentum / conservation_of_angular_momentum

aha_moment.statement: A steady torque does not set the speed — it sets how the speed changes.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The drive wheel presses in at a constant force while omega climbs past 2.00, 3.00, past 5.00 and never settles; alpha stays constant at +0.50.

scene_composition.text: The turntable spins steadily, no torque acting
tau reads 0.00, alpha reads 0.00, omega never changes
a turning push about the axle — right now there is none

tts_sentences.text_en: This turntable spins steadily, with two equal masses out on the rod.
Torque tau is a turning push about the axle — right now there is none.
Angular acceleration alpha is how quickly the spin rate changes each second.
With no torque, alpha stays at zero, and the spin rate omega never changes.

misconception_watch.belief: A spinning object slows and stops on its own; keeping it spinning needs a torque.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Torque tau reads 0.00 the whole state, and the spin-rate omega readout sits pinned at 1.50 rad/s for the whole state, never once dipping.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: With no net torque, alpha is zero — the spin neither grows nor dies; it continues.

STATE_2.title: Torque On: Spin Rate Keeps Rising

scene_composition.text: The motor drive wheel presses onto the rim
omega climbs past 2, past 3, never settling — alpha stays constant
like steadily pushing a playground merry-go-round

tts_sentences.text_en: The drive wheel touches the rim, turning.
Two point seven eight newtons at zero point five five metres gives one point five three newton-metres.
The push stays constant, but the spin rate keeps climbing — never settling.
That steady number is angular acceleration alpha, not the spin rate.
Like pushing a playground merry-go-round.

misconception_watch.belief: A constant torque makes it turn at a constant speed.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The drive wheel presses steadily and its rim arrow holds perfectly constant while omega climbs past 2.00, 3.00, 4.00 and never settles; the CONSTANT readout is alpha, not omega.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Torque sets the rate of CHANGE of spin — constant torque means constantly increasing speed.

scene_composition.text: The drive wheel is still pressing on, at first
wheel pulls back, tau and alpha drop to zero, omega holds
removing torque removes the change, not the motion

tts_sentences.text_en: The drive wheel is still pressing on, and the spin rate omega climbs toward six point five six.
Now the wheel pulls back — the push is gone.
Torque tau and angular acceleration alpha both drop to zero.
The spin rate omega does not fall — it holds exactly where the push left it.

scene_composition.text: A fresh run, from rest, masses moved in
I = 1.50: half for the frame, half for each mass
tau = I alpha predicts omega = 1.20 after 3 s — and it does

tts_sentences.text_en: A fresh run, from rest, masses moved in.
I is one point five oh: half for the frame, half for each mass.
One point oh nine newtons at the rim gives zero point six oh newton-metres.
Tau equals I times alpha: alpha is zero point four oh; omega reaches one point two oh.

scene_composition.text: Run A: from rest, omega reaches 1.25
same torque, masses moved in — run B reaches 5.80 in the same time
like riders near a merry-go-round's edge

tts_sentences.text_en: From rest, run A reaches omega of one point two five.
Masses move in to point two oh; same torque, again.
In the same two point five seconds, run B reaches omega of five point eight oh.
Smaller I means alpha is four point six four times larger.
Like riders near a merry-go-round's edge.

misconception_watch.belief: The same torque always produces the same acceleration — only how much mass, not where it sits.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Identical drive wheel, identical tau = 1.53, equal 2.5 s drives — run B (masses near the axle) reaches 5.80 in the time run A reached 1.25; alpha reads 2.32 versus run A's 0.50.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: alpha = tau/I, and I depends on where the mass sits — 4.64x less inertia, 4.64x more acceleration.

scene_composition.text: The brake pad presses in, touching the rim
alpha turns negative, omega falls to zero, then holds
friction only slows a spin, never reverses it

tts_sentences.text_en: The brake pad presses in, touching the rim.
Torque tau now opposes the spin: alpha turns negative, and omega falls steadily to zero.
At rest, the pad holds the wheel still — tau reads zero, matching alpha.
This brake is friction: it only slows a spin, never reverses it — a driven torque could.

scene_composition.text: Newton's second law, per particle
each mass needs 0.80 N; torque per mass 0.64 N*m; frame 0.25 N*m

tts_sentences.text_en: Newton's second law, per particle: force equals mass times r times alpha.
Each mass needs zero point eight oh newtons of tangential force.
That torque is zero point six four newton-metres for each mass.
The frame adds zero point two five the same way — total one point five three, exactly I alpha.

scene_composition.text: Everything is live now
drag torque, r, mass, starting speed — watch alpha follow instantly
tau_net = I alpha

tts_sentences.text_en: Now drag the torque, the radius, the mass or the starting speed yourself — watch alpha and omega answer live, and try the brake against the drive together.

regeneration_variants.label: Spinning Up a Potter's Wheel
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A potter's foot keeps a steady push on the flywheel — the wheel does not settle at one speed, it keeps speeding up for as long as the push continues.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical proportion: the same steady torque produces a constant angular acceleration, never a constant speed; moving clay farther from the centre raises I and slows the spin-up for the same push.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same turntable rig, same physics — the motor drive wheel is relabeled as a foot pedal driving a potter's flywheel.

regeneration_variants.label: Pedalling a Bicycle Wheel on a Stand
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A steady pedal force on a bicycle wheel mounted on a stand makes the wheel speed up continuously, not settle at one rate — and the same pedal force spins a wheel with a heavier rim more slowly.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same rotational second law: torque sets the rate of change of spin, and moment of inertia (mass distribution) modulates how much a given torque changes the spin rate.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same rig, same physics — the drive wheel is relabeled as a pedal chain-ring driving a mounted bicycle wheel.

STATE_1.caption: No torque: spin rate unchanged

STATE_2.label: A constant drive torque does not set the speed — it sets how fast the speed changes
STATE_2.caption: Torque on: spin rate climbs

STATE_3.label: Removing the torque removes the change, not the motion — omega holds where the push left it
STATE_3.caption: Torque off: spin rate stays

STATE_4.label: The equation tau = I alpha predicts the outcome before the run, exactly
STATE_4.caption: Equation predicts the speed

STATE_5.label: The same torque gives less alpha when I is bigger — two runs, same tau, different r
STATE_5.caption: More inertia: less acceleration

STATE_6.label: A friction brake torque is a negative alpha: omega falls at a steady rate, then friction holds it at rest
STATE_6.caption: Brake on: negative alpha

STATE_7.label: The law is Newton's second law summed over the body's particles: tau = (Sigma m r^2) alpha = I alpha
STATE_7.caption: Adding up every particle

formula_lines.text: τ = (Σ m r²) α = I α = 1.53 N·m
